title: Choose NextKid’s visual world
question: I recommend Match Card. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Match Card
options.lineage: weatherproof referee notebooks and match-day roster cards
options.thesis: A living touchline ledger makes arrival order, placement, and the next fair swap readable in one glance.
options.viewport: A match header and explicit clock sit above one decisive swap strip, with two compact field ledgers and the bench completing the screen.
options.risk: It can feel administrative if the player strips lack the snap and scale of real sideline notation.

options.label: Touchline Wayfinding
options.thesis: The interface is a chain of decisions, showing coaches only the next substitution route with monumental clarity.
options.case: Wins pure decision clarity; loses some soccer-specific identity to the recommended match-card world.
options.viewport: A giant OUT → IN instruction dominates, followed by destination-style field bands and an explicit clock direction.
options.risk: The airport metaphor can overpower the people and warmth of a children’s game.

options.label: Live Rotation Board
options.thesis: Every player is a live row whose rank and location visibly update across both coaches’ phones.
options.case: Makes shared live state unmistakable; the dense black board is less natural in bright outdoor light.
options.viewport: A ranked next-swap row sits above fixed FIELD A, FIELD B, and BENCH columns that cascade when a player moves.
options.risk: Condensed rows can make children feel like schedule data and reduce sunny-day legibility.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A polished conventional lineup screen with green field cards, player chips, and standard controls.
canonCard.viewport: A top bar and timer sit above two green field cards and a horizontally grouped bench.
canonCard.risk: It is immediately familiar but does little to sharpen the unique normalized-fairness decision.
